Additive API compatibility review: preserve the pinned 2ab52e819537faf30c1f63116c4705dbb4aeab53 / 0.2.0 baseline and BinaryAndSourceCompatible intention. Retain unfiltered backward MiMa and existing TASTy-MiMa courts. Forward MiMa is an approximation for source compatibility and reports new classes/methods as absent from the old artifact. Accept only the exact 79 reviewed additions in compatibility/interaction-additions.txt (76 emitted classes in the new intaglio.interaction namespace, plus the distinct Plot.addPackagedLayer method and two package-private compiler/type-witness hooks). Existing constructors and existing method signatures are unchanged; the failed overloaded addLayer design was replaced earlier by a distinct method.

Guardrails implemented in project/InteractionCompatibility.scala: exact SHA/version match, no wildcard symbols, candidate/baseline class-presence checks, stale-review rejection against actual forward findings, and compiled negative fixtures using the actual MiMa engine. Calibration proves the reviewed class/method additions are filtered only in the forward path while an unreviewed class, unreviewed method, and removed legacy method remain detected. Public examples compiled via docs/mdoc: 49 files, zero errors. Interaction compiler suites now pass 42 cases on each platform, including custom-stat rows with adversarial equality and a source-key mutation rejection.

Cross-project setting correction: initial top-level coreJVM / mimaForwardIssueFilters did not survive effective project settings. Moved the review into core.jvmSettings and verified inspect coreJVM/mimaForwardIssueFilters names build.sbt and the expected artifact dependencies. A new complete isolated-baseline run is active in process handle 10918, log /private/tmp/intaglio-interaction-compatibility-final.log. Do not claim it passed until its terminal result is checked. The preceding failed logs are retained. This review is not a universal Scala source-compatibility proof; documented examples, typed tests, TASTy, binary checks, and renderer evidence remain separate.
